## File Preview Router (FP)

The preview slot the four format shells project into — and the reason a shell never has to know what a PDF is.

```gts
<FilePreviewStage @model={{viewModel}} @format='isolated' @fields={{@fields}} />
```

### What the stage owns, so no family has to

- the **current-render cache**
- the **loading** and **failure** panes
- **provenance** and **staleness** signals — whether what you are looking at came from the source bytes or from something derived, and whether it is still current
- the generic pane for a family with no renderer yet

Everything else is handed to `static previewComponent` on the FileDef subclass.

### Two signatures, deliberately different

`FilePreviewSignature` is the shell-facing face: `{ model: FileViewModel, format, fields }`. The `format` arg tells the renderer which budget it is under — `fitted` is the collection cell, `embedded` and `isolated` may show complete content.

`ContentPreviewSignature` is the content-only face for the components the `file-formats/index` barrel exports (`MarkdownPreview`, `ImagePreview`, `AudioPreview`): just the content, no shell chrome — no file bar, no inspector, no Download or Copy-link. An embedding author who imports one of those **owns the loading, failure and staleness states themselves**, because the stage is not there to draw them.

### The projection trap

`ContentPreviewSignature.model` accepts either the FileDef instance (the common case — the component projects it through `fileViewModel` itself) or a **prebuilt** `FileViewModel`, which is what the shells pass.

A prebuilt view model must have been projected **at the same format** you then pass as `format`. Fitted budgets are applied at projection time, so a complete-content projection rendered at `'fitted'` would feed the whole file to the snippet branch. A consumer that varies `format` should pass the instance and let the component re-project.

### `fields` is a delegation hatch, not a data bag

The host format component's `@fields` is threaded through so a family renderer can delegate to a declared field's own component — a `MarkdownField` viewer, say — instead of re-implementing that rendering.

### The family this belongs to

Five pieces make up how a file renders in Boxel:

| Piece | Job |
|---|---|
| `file-shell-atom` | inline reference — icon, name, extension |
| `file-shell-embedded` | complete content, flowing inside a document |
| `file-shell-fitted` | the parent-sized collection cell |
| `file-shell-isolated` | the full work surface |
| `file-preview-stage` | the slot all four project into; owns loading, failure, provenance |

A shell never knows how to draw a PDF, a waveform or a 3D scene. It renders the
stage, and the stage hands the remaining space to the family's own renderer,
declared by a FileDef subclass as `static previewComponent`. A file whose family
has no renderer yet gets an honest generic pane rather than a broken one.
